task_description: Write a method in Dafny to reverse each string in a given list of string values.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method ReverseStringsInList(strings: seq<string>) returns (reversed: seq<string>)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The length of the returned sequence is equal to the length of the input sequence
- Each string in the returned sequence is the reverse of the corresponding string in the input sequence
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.  
In this case:  
    method ReverseStringsInList(strings: seq<string>) returns (reversedList: seq<string>)  

Step 2: Determine the preconditions.  
In this case:  
Natural language description:  
    - There are no preconditions; the input list can be any sequence of strings.  

Dafny specification:  
    // No requires clause needed as the method works for any sequence of strings  

Step 3: Determine the postconditions.  
In this case:  
Natural language description:  
    - The output list has the same length as the input list  
    - Each string in the output list is the reverse of the corresponding string in the input list  

Dafny specification:  
    ensures |reversedList| == |strings|  
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |strings| ==> reversedList[i] == ReverseString(strings[i])  

Where ReverseString is a helper function that returns the reversed version of a string.

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.  

```dafny
// Helper function to reverse a string
function ReverseString(s: string): string
    decreases s
{
    if |s| == 0 then ""
    else ReverseString(s[1..]) + s[0..1]
}

method ReverseStringsInList(strings: seq<string>) returns (reversedList: seq<string>)
    ensures |reversedList| == |strings|
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |strings| ==> reversedList[i] == ReverseString(strings[i])
{
    var result := [];
    var i := 0;
    while i < |strings|
        invariant 0 <= i <= |strings|
        invariant |result| == i
        invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> result[j] == ReverseString(strings[j])
    {
        result := result + [ReverseString(strings[i])];
        i := i + 1;
    }
    return result;
}
```
